headline: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 model suite with Sol, Terra, Luna
summary: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 with three models for coding, cybersecurity, and biology. GPT-5.6 Sol costs $5 input / $30 output per million tokens.
details: OpenAI has unveiled the limited preview of its new GPT 5.6 model suite, which includes three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. Sol is the flagship model, Terra is a medium-tier model for 'high-volume work', and Luna is a 'fast and affordable' everyday model.
GPT-5.6 Sol is priced at $5 input / $30 output per million tokens, nearly half the cost of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5. Terra is half the cost of Sol, and Luna is less than half the cost of Terra.

The company says Sol is especially skilled at coding, cybersecurity, and biology, as well as staying focused during long-horizon agentic AI tasks. OpenAI also debuted two additional modes for Sol: a 'max' mode for deeper reasoning and an 'ultra' mode for leveraging sub-agents.

OpenAI dedicated the majority of its announcement blog post to safety and potential misuse, referencing the recent jailbreaking travails of its rival Anthropic. The company says Sol 'is better at helping people find and fix vulnerabilities than reliably carrying out end-to-end attacks'.

The model suite should be generally available in the coming weeks, with the company cooperating with the US government ahead of this launch. OpenAI hopes this won't be the norm for future model releases.
caption:
What just dropped in AI? OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 model suite!

OpenAI has unveiled the limited preview of its new GPT 5.6 model suite, which includes three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. Sol is the flagship model, Terra is a medium-tier model for 'high-volume work', and Luna is a 'fast and affordable' everyday model.

GPT-5.6 Sol is priced at $5 input / $30 output per million tokens, nearly half the cost of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5. Terra is half the cost of Sol, and Luna is less than half the cost of Terra.

The company says Sol is especially skilled at coding, cybersecurity, and biology, as well as staying focused during long-horizon agentic AI tasks. OpenAI also debuted two additional modes for Sol: a 'max' mode for deeper reasoning and an 'ultra' mode for leveraging sub-agents.

OpenAI dedicated the majority of its announcement blog post to safety and potential misuse, referencing the recent jailbreaking travails of its rival Anthropic. The company says Sol 'is better at helping people find and fix vulnerabilities than reliably carrying out end-to-end attacks'.

The model suite should be generally available in the coming weeks, with the company cooperating with the US government ahead of this launch. OpenAI hopes this won't be the norm for future model releases.
